question: What is the main goal of mental health promotion?

options.A: Building positive emotional strength and well-being
options.B: Treating severe psychiatric disorders with medication
options.C: Managing acute crisis behaviors in the emergency room
options.D: Discharging stable patients back into the community

explanation: Mental health promotion focuses on enhancing overall emotional well-being and psychological strength rather than treating existing illness. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h1)

question: How does prevention differ from traditional treatment in nursing?

options.A: Prevention stops illness before it starts, while treatment fixes existing problems
options.B: Prevention happens in hospitals, while treatment happens at home
options.C: Prevention uses only medication, while treatment uses talk therapy
options.D: Prevention is only done by doctors, while treatment is done by nurses

explanation: Prevention aims to intercept risk factors before a disorder develops, whereas traditional treatment addresses illness that is already present. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h1)

question: Which nursing action is an example of secondary prevention?

options.A: Running a stress-reduction workshop for healthy adults
options.B: Screening high school students for early signs of depression
options.C: Administering emergency life support for a drug overdose
options.D: Providing long-term rehabilitation for chronic schizophrenia

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and prompt treatment to stop mild symptoms from becoming severe disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h2)

question: A nurse leads a support group to help patients with chronic bipolar disorder prevent relapse. What level of prevention is this?
explanation: Tertiary prevention involves managing established, chronic conditions to reduce disability and prevent worsening or relapse. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h2)

question: What is a protective factor for mental health?

options.A: Strong family and social support systems
options.B: A family history of severe psychiatric illness
options.D: Growing up in an environment of chronic poverty

explanation: Protective factors like social support help shield individuals from stress and lower the likelihood of mental health problems. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h3)

question: Why can two people with similar childhood trauma have very different mental health outcomes?

options.A: Trauma only affects physical health, not emotional well-being
options.B: Medication can completely erase the memory of past trauma
options.C: Childhood trauma never leads to adult mental health problems
options.D: Differences in their individual protective factors and resilience

explanation: The presence of protective factors, coping skills, and supportive environments can buffer the impact of risk factors like trauma. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h3)

question: Who is the target audience for a universal mental health intervention?

options.A: Specific subgroups who share a high risk for a condition
options.B: Only people who have been diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder
options.C: An entire general population without checking individual risk
options.D: Individuals who show early, mild symptoms of mental illness

explanation: Universal interventions are delivered to everyone in a group or community regardless of their personal risk level. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h4)

question: A nurse provides a targeted stress management program specifically for children whose parents are going through a bitter divorce. What type of intervention is this?
explanation: Selective interventions target subgroups of the population that face a significantly higher risk of developing a problem due to specific life events. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h4)

question: Which statement best describes human resilience?

options.A: It only appears during old age and retirement years
options.B: It is a skill set and capacity that can be developed over time
options.C: It is a fixed genetic trait that cannot be changed after childhood
options.D: It means a person never feels stress or emotional pain

explanation: Resilience is dynamic; individuals can learn and strengthen their coping skills and emotional flexibility throughout their lives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h5)

question: An adult patient is overwhelmed by job loss and financial stress. Which nursing intervention best helps build resilience?

options.A: Teaching structured problem-solving and healthy emotional coping methods
options.B: Recommending that the patient avoid all future employment opportunities
options.C: Encouraging the patient to isolate until all financial problems are solved
options.D: Telling the patient to ignore the stress because things always work out

explanation: Teaching actionable problem-solving and healthy coping empowers patients to face crises constructively and builds long-term resilience. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h5)

question: Why is early identification and screening vital in psychiatric nursing?

options.A: It guarantees that patients will never experience stress again
options.B: It prevents mild symptoms from progressing into severe disorders
options.C: It replaces the need for physical health examinations
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any prescription medications

explanation: Early screening identifies issues while they are still manageable, reducing the likelihood of severe impairment or crisis. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h6)

question: Which action should a nurse take when conducting a mental health screening in a community clinic?

options.A: Build trusting rapport and explain the purpose of the screening questions
options.B: Diagnosing the patient with a psychiatric disorder immediately on the spot
options.C: Rushing through the questions so the patient does not feel uncomfortable
options.D: Ignoring non-verbal cues and focusing strictly on the written score

explanation: Establishing trust and explaining the purpose of screening helps reduce anxiety and encourages honest answers from the patient. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h6)

question: What is a major advantage of community-based mental health programs?

options.A: They completely remove the need for any professional medical staff
options.B: They require patients to live inside locked hospital facilities
options.C: They keep patients connected to their families and local neighborhoods
options.D: They eliminate all symptoms of mental illness permanently

explanation: Community-based care allows individuals to receive treatment while staying integrated in their daily social and family environments. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a typical duty of a nurse working in a community mental health center?

options.B: Performing major neurosurgery for treatment-resistant depression
options.C: Connecting vulnerable clients with local housing and food resources
options.D: Providing psychoeducation to patients and their family members

explanation: Nurses in community settings do not perform neurosurgery; their role focuses on support, education, medication management, and resource linkage. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h7)

question: What does mental health advocacy by nurses primarily involve?

options.A: Prescribing psychiatric medications without consulting a doctor
options.B: Isolating psychiatric patients from the general community
options.C: Challenging public stigma and fighting for fair health policies
options.D: Reducing hospital budgets by cutting nursing staff numbers

explanation: Nursing advocacy focuses on speaking up for patient rights, reducing stigma, and pushing for better mental health policies and funding. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h8)

question: Why is nurse-led advocacy essential for the prevention of mental health disorders?

options.A: Nurses can influence public policy and secure funding for community prevention programs
options.B: Nurses have the legal authority to pass national laws without legislative voting
options.C: Lawmakers only listen to nurses and ignore all other healthcare professionals
options.D: Advocacy replaces the need for direct clinical care in hospitals

explanation: Nurses use their frontline experience and health data to convince leaders to invest resources into preventive mental health initiatives. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h8)
